why: Two graph ideas chained: first find which vertices lie on a cycle by peeling leaves (repeatedly delete degree-1 vertices; what survives is the cycle), then run one multi-source BFS from all cycle vertices to get each vertex's distance to its cycle.
hints: A vertex of degree 1 can never be on a cycle. Delete it; does that create new degree-1 vertices?
Keep removing degree-1 vertices with a queue until none are left. In a graph where each component has one cycle, exactly the cycle vertices remain.
Seed a BFS with every surviving vertex at distance 0 and spread outward; the level each removed vertex is reached at is its answer. O(n).
pitfalls: Recursive DFS for cycle finding overflows at 2 * 10^5 vertices in Python; leaf peeling avoids recursion.
Several components each have their own cycle; seeding all cycle vertices at once handles them together.
